content.text: The verifier's feedback affirms every substantive element of the finding — status, direction, cited evidence, the distinction of the two Vendor-side access items, and the treatment of the regex as a false signal. There is no substantive defect to repair, and the one "failed" item is the deterministic check the verifier itself confirms cannot match. Re-submitting the compliant finding unchanged in substance; adding a redline here would be affirmatively harmful.

input.quote: e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against the Client anywhere in this Agreement, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access parameter to cap and no redline is warranted. Confirmed by keyword searches returning no hits for audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises, examine and review, and by full reads of the fee provisions (SS 5-6), Client covenants (S 8), the license grant (S 2) and confidentiality (S 10). Every information flow runs in our favour: S 3(e) gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, and S 6 entitles Client to documentation supporting charges plus a right to contest them, so TrueLink has no contractual hook for a usage audit. The two Vendor-side access items are not audit rights: S 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and S 9 requires Client access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, at Client's request. Neither grants remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is absent. The failed deterministic check for an audit-frequency limit is a false signal: the pattern cannot match because no audit clause exists to limit, and silence is more favourable to us than the preferred position. Inserting frequency, notice and cost parameters would require first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe, so we take no action. Retained as internal negotiation discipline rather than a raised issue: if TrueLink later proposes a verification right, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent, and no direct access to Client systems. Residual caveat: SS 5-6 contain unfilled fee blanks and reference Exhibits A and B, which are not in the extracted text; if those exhibits carry a reporting or verification mechanic, this rule should be re-run against them.
